issues.legal_issue: A government may not propose substantial modifications to a development plan unless it forms the required opinion that the modifications are necessary on the basis of relevant material, and that opinion is open to limited judicial review.
material_facts: A development plan had reserved the owners’ land for an educational purpose, but the responsible authority did not acquire it, and an earlier attempt to continue the reservation had been set aside.

When the government proposed a new educational designation through substantial modifications to the revised plan, the available record included planning advice and a note recommending that the land be placed in a residential zone.
The record did not disclose relevant material supporting the new designation or the government’s formation of an opinion that substantial modifications were necessary.
The preliminary notification did not reflect such an opinion; the government’s asserted public-interest rationale appeared later in a reply affidavit.
issues.conclusion: The preliminary and final notifications designating the land for educational use were ultra vires and void. The owners could use the land for residential purposes, and the authorities were directed to take the necessary steps without creating further obstacles.
issues.legal_principle: Under Sections 17(1)(a)(ii) and 21 of the Gujarat Town Planning and Urban Development Act, 1976, the power to propose substantial modifications to a development plan is conditional on the State Government forming an opinion that the modifications are necessary. Although that opinion is subjective, relevant material must exist to support it, and the decision must reflect consideration of relevant aspects. A court may examine whether that material exists and has a rational connection to the opinion, and whether the opinion is arbitrary, capricious, whimsical, or based on extraneous grounds; it does not assess the sufficiency of the material as if forming the opinion itself. A later affidavit cannot supply a rationale absent from the public notification and contemporaneous record. The Court relied on Barium Chemicals Ltd. v. Company Law Board, Income-tax Officer, Calcutta v. Lakhmani Mewal Das, J. Jayalalitha v. Union of India, Gordhandas Bhanji, and Mohinder Singh Gill v. Chief Election Commissioner. It also applied the principle from Bhavnagar University v. Palitana Sugar Mill that restrictions on land use and statutory interference with property rights must be construed strictly.

rule.if: plan_modification_challenge and substantial_modification_proposed and (no_relevant_material_support or no_necessity_opinion_formed)

predicates.plan_modification_challenge: A person challenged a government action proposing a substantial modification to a development plan.
predicates.substantial_modification_proposed: The government proposed a substantial change to the development plan.
predicates.no_relevant_material_support: The contemporaneous record contained no relevant material supporting the proposed change.
predicates.no_necessity_opinion_formed: The government did not form an opinion, based on relevant material, that the substantial change was necessary.
predicates.substantial_modification_is_void: The proposed substantial modification is invalid.

issues.definition: When a challenge concerns a proposed substantial plan modification, the modification is invalid if relevant material does not support it or the government has not formed the required opinion that it is necessary.
